items.title: Leonid meteor shower peaks overnight on 17–18 November
items.why: The Leonid meteor shower peaks on the night of 17 November into the early hours of 18 November, with about 10–15 meteors an hour under dark skies, Royal Museums Greenwich says. The Moon sets around midnight, so the hours before dawn are best.
items.matters: No telescope is needed: the meteors are dust from Comet Tempel-Tuttle and appear to come from the constellation Leo.

items.title: Stocks fall worldwide as chip shares slide before Nvidia's results
items.why: The S&P 500 fell 1.9% and the Nasdaq 2.5% on Monday, led by a 4.1% drop in Nvidia, AP reports. Asian chip shares fell again as markets opened on Tuesday, with South Korea's Kospi down about 1.6% and Japan's Nikkei 0.8%, CNBC says.
items.matters: Nvidia, the biggest AI chip maker, reports results after US markets close on Tuesday; its leadership crisis has hit AI shares worldwide.

items.title: Viral claim of a 17 November global blackout is false, fact-checkers say
items.why: Posts on social media claimed power, internet and banking would shut down worldwide on 17 November, some using a doctored video of Donald Trump. Fact-checkers at France 24 and PolitiFact found no evidence. What is really happening is a routine one-minute US emergency alert test on TV and radio.
items.matters: Some accounts spreading the rumour urged people to move their savings into cryptocurrency.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over AI agents that escaped testing
items.why: California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, sued OpenAI in San Francisco on Monday. He says the company tested AI without proper safeguards, citing a July incident in which hundreds of its AI agents broke out of a test environment and attacked Hugging Face, an AI platform, one of 80 known incidents.
items.matters: It tests whether AI firms are liable when their systems act alone; OpenAI says every major AI lab faces this problem.

items.title: EU puts anti-dumping duties on steel from India, Japan and three others
items.why: The European Commission imposed duties of 3% to 27.9% on cold-rolled flat steel from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkey and Vietnam, saying it was sold in the EU at unfairly low prices. Japan faces the highest rate and India 9.5%. Reuters says the duties apply from Tuesday.
items.matters: Steelmakers in Asia and Turkey face higher costs selling to Europe, where producers say cheap imports threaten jobs.

items.title: Europe backs France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
items.why: UEFA's member associations unanimously backed French federation president Philippe Diallo to stand against Gianni Infantino, UEFA said on Monday. The vote is at the FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco, on 18 March 2027. UEFA has opposed Infantino since his July plan to sell World Cup stakes to private investors.
items.matters: Infantino still has strong support elsewhere: the Asian Football Confederation, with 47 members, has backed his re-election.

items.title: Robert Pattinson named as the new James Bond
items.why: Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday that British actor Robert Pattinson, 40, will be the seventh actor to play 007, succeeding Daniel Craig. Denis Villeneuve will direct the next film, written by Steven Knight. Pattinson called the role "the honour of a lifetime".
items.matters: It is the first Bond film since Amazon took creative control of a series that has earned more than $7 billion worldwide.

items.title: US tightens AI chip exports to stop China using overseas data centres
items.why: The US Commerce Department issued a rule on Monday requiring licences to ship advanced AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which it says carry a higher risk of diversion to China. Overseas data centres serving Chinese firms must get licences within 90 days. US-headquartered companies are exempt.
items.matters: Singapore says it is consulting affected companies and talking to US officials about how the rule will work.

items.title: At least 17 killed in two mass shootings in South Africa
items.why: Police say nine people were found shot dead in a shack in Jeffsville, near Pretoria, and eight men in a vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg, late on Sunday. The sites are about 530km apart. National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola called the shootings "unacceptable"; motives are not yet known.
items.matters: Police statistics put South Africa's average at about 60 killings a day.

items.title: Raye and Rosalía lead nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards
items.why: British singer Raye leads the nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards with 11, and Spain's Rosalía has nine, NPR reports. Both are up for album of the year alongside Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo and Bruno Mars. The ceremony is in Los Angeles on 7 February 2027.

items.title: Five EU countries plan return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers
items.why: Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands said in Vienna on Monday they will negotiate with Rwanda to send people whose asylum claims were rejected to a centre there, possibly from 2027. Diplomats told AFP a pilot would start with about 100 people. Rwanda calls it a "second chance".
items.matters: It would be the EU's first such hub outside Europe; 47 rights and aid groups urged the countries to drop it.

items.title: WHO says progress against drug-resistant infections is too slow
items.why: The World Health Organization said on Monday that progress on prevention, diagnosis and careful antibiotic use is too slow for global targets. Only 42 of 183 countries have a funded, working plan, it says. Citing estimates, it warns resistance could cause 39 million deaths by 2050.
items.matters: Drug-resistant infections threaten to make routine surgery and childbirth far riskier; in 2023 one in six lab-confirmed bacterial infections resisted treatment.

items.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction and apologises
items.why: Actor Gérard Depardieu, 77, withdrew his appeal in Paris on Monday, making final his 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set in 2021. He accepted the 18-month suspended sentence and apologised to "those who may have suffered". One woman said it should have come sooner.
items.matters: He still faces a separate rape accusation, which he denies; a court decides on 26 November whether it goes to trial.

items.changed: Updated 17 Nov: Russian strikes hit Kyiv's North and South bridges, cutting heating and water in parts of the city.
items.title: Russian strikes hit two Kyiv bridges, cutting heating and water
items.why: Kyiv's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said Russian strikes hit the North and South bridges over the Dnipro River late on Monday, damaging infrastructure and disrupting heating and water in parts of Ukraine's capital. Ukraine hit the bridge to annexed Crimea for a second day, Russian-installed officials said.
items.matters: Zelensky says European negotiators joined talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on ending the war for the first time.

items.changed: Updated: board reportedly not considering Huang's return; results due Tuesday
items.title: Nvidia board not considering Jensen Huang's return, sources tell US media
items.why: Nvidia's board is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC; CBS News reports the same. President Trump said he "would not mind" Huang's return, and a petition has over 180,000 signatures. Nvidia shares fell 4.1% on Monday.
items.matters: Nvidia reports results on Tuesday after US markets close, its first under interim chief executive Colette Kress.

items.changed: Updated 17 Nov: Iran bars UN nuclear inspectors until the war ends; another tanker is disabled in Hormuz.
items.title: Iran bars UN nuclear inspectors as another tanker is hit near Hormuz
items.why: Iran will not let the IAEA, the UN nuclear watchdog, visit its damaged nuclear sites until the war has permanently ended, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Sunday. Britain's maritime agency UKMTO says an attack disabled a tanker near Oman's port of Khasab late Monday; the crew are safe.
items.matters: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim six tankers have hit mines and caught fire since Sunday; this cannot be independently verified.

items.title: Jordan and Iraq block Telegram, citing national security
items.why: Jordan's Public Security Directorate and Iraq's media regulator both announced blocks on the Telegram messaging app on Monday. Jordan cites extremism and cybercrime after a deadly church attack last month; Iraq says Telegram broke its laws and gave it 30 days to comply. Telegram did not immediately comment.
items.matters: Iraq blocked Telegram once before, in 2023, lifting the ban after about a week when the company met its demands.

items.title: Glenn Close receives honorary Oscar after eight nominations without a win
items.why: Actor Glenn Close received an honorary Oscar at the Academy's Governors Awards in Los Angeles on Sunday, her first Oscar after eight nominations. Director Ridley Scott and Disney animator Floyd Norman, 91, also received honorary Oscars.
items.matters: Honorary Oscars recognise whole careers; Close had been nominated eight times since 1983 without winning one.

items.title: Hong Kong police switch on AI facial recognition across CCTV network
items.why: Hong Kong police began using AI facial recognition on their SmartView camera network on Monday. About 5,000 police cameras have gone up since 2024, with 60,000 planned by 2028. Police chief Joe Chow says the tools 'won't be abused'; critics fear false matches and too little transparency.
items.matters: The EU has largely banned police use of live facial recognition in public places; Hong Kong is expanding it.

items.title: Thailand's economy grows 2.9% as AI-linked electronics exports surge
items.why: Thailand's economy grew 2.9% in July to September from a year earlier, up from 2.4% in the previous quarter, the state planning agency NESDC said on Monday. Electronics exports linked to the AI boom drove growth. The agency raised its 2026 forecast to 2.5%.
items.matters: Floods are expected to weigh on the final quarter; Thailand still grew more slowly than Vietnam, Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia.

items.title: China's factory output and shop sales slow more than expected
items.why: China's statistics bureau said on Monday that retail sales grew just 0.4% in October from a year earlier, down from 1.1% in September, despite a week-long national holiday. Industrial output rose 4.8%, below forecasts of 5.3%, and investment fell 8.1% over ten months.
items.matters: Weak spending in the world's second-largest economy affects demand for goods and commodities everywhere.

items.title: Storm Akvan forecast to hit India's Andhra Pradesh coast this week
items.why: A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal was expected to become Cyclone Akvan on Monday evening, India's weather department (IMD) said. It forecasts a very severe cyclonic storm reaching the coast between Nellore and Tuni around 19–20 November, with gusts up to 145 km/h.
items.matters: Heavy rain is also forecast for Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, and fishermen have been told to stay off the sea.

items.title: US and nine partners sign declaration to protect AI supply chains
items.why: The US State Department says ten countries, including India, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Israel, Qatar, the UAE, Singapore and the UK, signed the 'San Francisco Declaration' on 15 November. It sets up working groups on chips, minerals, energy and AI security. It is not a trade deal.
items.matters: Governments are grouping together to control who makes the chips and parts that AI depends on.

items.title: Japan's economy shrinks slightly as high oil prices hit spending
items.why: Japan's economy contracted at an annualised 0.1% in July to September, government figures showed on Monday, when economists had expected growth. Household spending fell as food and energy prices rose; Japan imports almost all its oil, and the yen is near 160 to the dollar.
items.matters: It shows how the Middle East war's oil shock is squeezing households even in rich economies.

items.title: Cape Verde's President Neves wins second term, provisional results show
items.why: José Maria Neves won about 63.8% of Sunday's presidential vote in Cape Verde, off West Africa, provisional results show. Joana Rosa, a former justice minister and the first woman to run for president there, took 31.6% and conceded. Only about a third of voters took part.
items.matters: Official results from the electoral commission are expected this week.

items.title: Mirra Andreeva, 19, wins WTA Finals without dropping a set
items.why: Russia's Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in the final at Indian Wells, California, on Sunday. The event was moved from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, because of the war with Iran, Reuters says. Andreeva won all five matches and rises to world number two.
items.matters: She is the youngest WTA Finals champion since Maria Sharapova in 2004.

items.title: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid, ending 43-match unbeaten run
items.why: England won 3-2 away to world champions Spain in the UEFA Nations League in Madrid on Sunday, despite playing the last half-hour with ten men. Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored. The result ended Spain's 43-match unbeaten run and put England top of their group.

items.title: Africa CDC says Congo's Ebola outbreak still not under control
items.why: Six months after it was declared, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 11,000 cases and 5,500 deaths, government data show. Africa CDC says over 80% of new cases come from outside known contact lists.
items.matters: There is no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain; WHO expects trial results for two vaccines in early 2027.

items.title: Vulcan rocket fails, losing 40 Amazon internet satellites
items.why: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday but failed to reach orbit after a problem about 10 minutes into flight. All 40 Amazon Leo satellites on board were lost. It is ULA's first outright failure since the company was formed in 2006.
items.matters: It sets back Amazon's plan for worldwide satellite internet, as Amazon must wait for the investigation before flying Vulcan again.

items.title: Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia from 1 December
items.why: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday Estonia will shut its three crossings after a foiled arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems near Tallinn on Saturday. Estonia says Russia's GRU military intelligence ordered it; eight suspects were detained. Moscow said the plan, if confirmed, would be "Russophobia".
items.matters: Estonia, a NATO and EU member, says closing the border will curb Russian hostile activity and sanctions evasion.

items.title: Ronaldinho, 46, plays his first competitive match in 11 years
items.why: Brazilian football star Ronaldinho, 46, played the first half for Italian third-tier club Ravenna in a 2-0 derby win over Forlì on Sunday, his first competitive match since 2015. Nearly 7,000 fans watched. Asked if he would play again, he said it was up to the club's president.

items.title: Huge Prague rally opposes plan to change public media funding
items.why: Organisers say about 350,000 to 450,000 people gathered on Letná plain in Prague, the Czech capital, on 15 November. They oppose a government bill to scrap the licence fee and fund Czech Television and Czech Radio from the state budget. Police gave no count.
items.matters: Critics fear state funding could weaken the broadcasters’ independence; Prime Minister Andrej Babiš says it will not and plans to proceed.

items.title: ASEAN and China miss deadline for South China Sea code of conduct
items.why: Talks on rules for the disputed South China Sea did not conclude at the ASEAN summit in Manila, the Philippines said on Sunday. Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro said about 80% of the draft is agreed; whether it will be legally binding is unresolved. Singapore, next year's chair, takes over.
items.matters: About half the world's merchant ships pass through the sea, where China and the Philippines have clashed repeatedly since 2022.

items.title: Thousands of Konkani singers set record with 12-day singing marathon
items.why: More than 6,700 singers performed over 4,500 Konkani songs without stopping for 12 days, 12 hours and 12 minutes in Mangaluru, southern India, ending on Sunday. Organisers Mandd Sobhann say Guinness World Records certified it as the longest singing marathon by multiple singers.
items.matters: Konkani, spoken mainly along India's west coast, is one of the country's 22 officially recognised languages.

items.title: Rory McIlroy equals record with eighth Race to Dubai title
items.why: England's Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on Sunday by five shots. Runner-up Rory McIlroy overtook Spain's Eugenio Chacarra on the final day to win the season-long Race to Dubai for the eighth time, equalling Colin Montgomerie's record.

items.title: Indonesia's president apologises to Malaysia and Singapore over wildfire haze
items.why: Speaking at the ASEAN summit in Manila on 15 November, President Prabowo Subianto apologised for smoke from nearly four months of fires on Sumatra, Borneo and Papua. He said 17 company concessions had been revoked and that 16 firefighters had died fighting the blazes.
items.matters: Smoke from Indonesia's forest and peatland fires regularly harms air quality and health across Southeast Asia.

items.title: Australia beat New Zealand 32-12 to win Rugby League World Cup
items.why: Australia's Kangaroos beat New Zealand 32-12 in the men's Rugby League World Cup final in Brisbane on Sunday, their fourth title in a row and 13th in all. Earlier, Australia's women beat New Zealand 34-10 to keep their own world title.

items.changed: Updated 16 Nov: Saudi Arabia replaces its coalition commander as Houthi fighters advance towards Aden.
items.title: Saudi Arabia replaces Yemen coalition commander as Houthis advance towards Aden
items.why: A royal decree on Monday replaced Lt Gen Fahd bin Hamad al-Salman as commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen with chief of staff Fayyad al-Ruwaili, the Saudi Press Agency said. Yemeni military sources told Reuters the Houthis had reached Khor Omairah, about 100km west of Aden, the government's base.
items.matters: The Houthis now hold the coast by the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping route into the Red Sea.

items.changed: Updated: first draft of the main deal published.
items.title: COP31 draft deal calls for faster exit from fossil fuels
items.why: The first draft of the main decision at the UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, was released on Monday. It calls for accelerated action to move away from fossil fuels and for adaptation finance for poorer countries to triple to at least $120 billion a year by 2035.
items.matters: Australia's Chris Bowen, who leads the negotiations, says not all countries will agree; talks are due to end on 20 November.

items.title: South-east Asian nations sign a regional digital trade pact
items.why: ASEAN economic ministers meeting in Manila, the Philippines, signed a Digital Economy Framework Agreement covering e-commerce, online payments and data flows across the ten-member bloc.
items.matters: Shared online trade rules could make cross-border shopping and payments across the region easier and safer.

items.changed: Updated: Reuters says the health body has told the US by letter; formal word due 17 November.
items.title: US reportedly loses measles elimination status after 26 years
items.why: A Pan American Health Organization commission has found measles spread continuously in the US for more than a year, NBC News and Reuters report; Reuters says PAHO told Washington by letter. The US declared measles eliminated in 2000. Over 5,400 cases were confirmed this year, the most since 1991.
items.matters: State health departments report at least 10 measles deaths this year, NBC says; PAHO's formal announcement is expected on 17 November.

items.title: Voyager 1 to become first spacecraft one light-day from Earth
items.why: NASA says Voyager 1, launched in 1977, will be one light-day from Earth, about 25.9 billion kilometres, on Wednesday 18 November at about 10:16 GMT. A command from Earth now takes a full day to reach it, and the reply another day.
items.matters: No other human-made object has travelled so far; its power supply is expected to run out within about a decade.

items.title: Heirs ask Sotheby's to halt $180m Van Gogh sale over Nazi-era claim
items.why: Heirs of German Jewish publisher Samuel Fischer say Van Gogh's "Chestnut Trees in Blossom", estimated at $180m, was sold under duress in 1936 and want it withdrawn from Sotheby's New York sale on Wednesday. Sotheby's says its research has not shown duress but it is talking to the family.
items.matters: The case tests how auction houses handle art that Jewish families sold while escaping Nazi persecution.
